notes: Snap election called by PM Sanae Takaichi. LDP won historic two-thirds supermajority (316/465 seats), roaring back after 2024 money scandal losses. Takaichi became Japan's first elected woman PM with sweeping mandate for conservative policy agenda.
Constitutional Rewrite — Voters approved beginning the process of drafting a new constitution to replace the 2017 coup-era charter. YES won with 21.62M votes vs 11.24M NO.

Bhumjaithai Party emerged as surprise winner despite only leading caretaker government for 4 months. Constitutional referendum also held same day. Bhumjaithai formed coalition with Pheu Thai. Described as a shock result and complete upset.

BNP won majority. Awami League boycotted. Elections followed August 2024 student-led protests that ousted PM Sheikh Hasina. UPDATE Jul 24 2026: President Mohammed Shahabuddin (Hasina ally, in office since Apr 2023) resigned citing health (Autonomic Neuropathy). Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad acting as president. New president must be elected within 90 days. Hasina (sentenced to death in absentia) has stated intent to return from India exile in December 2026. Sources: BBC, Al Jazeera, Reuters, AP
July National Charter Reforms — Voters approved institutional governance reforms based on the July 2024 uprising demands (democratic safeguards, accountability measures).
RSP won 182/275 seats. Nepali Congress 38, CPN-UML 25. First time a new party won majority. Shah became youngest PM in Nepal history.

Greens narrowly held power. Ozdemir (former federal agriculture minister) succeeded Kretschmann. CDU came within 0.6 points. AfD doubled its 2021 result to ~20%. SPD hit record low. Left Party entered parliament for first time. Sources: DW, OSW, GMF
CDU ended 35 years of continuous SPD rule in Rhineland-Palatinate. AfD gained over 10 percentage points. Major blow to SPD as junior coalition partner in federal government. Sources: DW, OSW, KAS
Historic election ending 16 years of Fidesz rule. TISZA won two-thirds supermajority (53% vs 39%). Magyar became PM in May 2026. EU unlocked 16.4B euros in frozen funds.

Early parliamentary election (8th since 2021). Progressive Bulgaria won 131/240 seats (outright majority). Former President Radev resigned Jan 2026 to form party. Triggered by collapse of GERB coalition after street protests. 24 parties contested, 4783 candidates.

incumbent: Various State CMs (Mamata Banerjee-WB, MK Stalin-TN, Pinarayi Vijayan-Kerala, Himanta Sarma-Assam)
notes: BJP won West Bengal for the first time in history, defeating Mamata Banerjee's TMC. Also won Bihar and Assam. Suvendu Adhikari led BJP's state campaign. Turnout 93.71% in West Bengal (highest ever). Mamata filed election petition in Calcutta High Court. Tamil Nadu elections also held in this cycle.
PAICV unseated ruling MpD after a decade in power. Francisco Carvalho set to become PM. Five parties competed for 72 National Assembly seats.
Prosperity Party won another large parliamentary majority (landslide). Results released June 21. Election held June 1. Fears of new conflict persist. Sources: BBC, Reuters, RFI, DW Africa

First national election under President Lee Jae Myung. Democratic Party swept most regions but lost symbolic Seoul mayoral race to PPP. Elections for governors, mayors, local council members, and education superintendents. Protests erupted after results over election integrity claims.
Pashinyan won with 49.81% in closely contested election. Turnout ~59%. Pro-Western PM saw off Russian pressure.

Extremely close runoff (margin ~0.2%). First round held April 12 with 35 candidates. Fujimori becomes Peru's first elected female president (inauguration July 28). Sánchez refuses to recognize result, alleges fraud. Peru's 9th president in 10 years. Sources: Reuters, France 24, Al Jazeera, AS/COA
Population cap initiative (No to 10 Million) rejected 52.82% to 47.18%. Civilian Service Act amendment also voted on.

Extremely close runoff (margin <1%). De la Espriella, a former criminal lawyer nicknamed "the Tiger," was endorsed by U.S. President Trump. First round held May 31 with 14 candidates. Cepeda conceded June 24 after initially challenging results. Marks a hard-right swing after Petro's leftist government. Sources: Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN, Americas Quarterly

Algeria held parliamentary elections on July 2, 2026 with historically low turnout of 21.24%. The ruling National Liberation Front (FLN) won 90 out of 407 seats, followed by RND and independents. Results announced July 6, 2026.

Referendum declared INVALID. Turnout 16.1% (required 50%). Two questions: (1) Cancel lifelong payments for PM Fico and leaders, 95% voted Yes; (2) Reopen Special Prosecutor Office and NAKA, 94% voted Yes. Organized by Democrats party after 350,000+ petition signatures. Fico SMER coalition boycotted. Only 1 of 10 referendums in Slovakia history (2003 EU membership) ever reached validity threshold. 99.98% of votes counted.

RESULT (Jul 20): Carlos Vila Nova wins second term with 55%+ of vote (preliminary). Nito D'Abreu (ADI) received 41%+. No runoff needed. Vila Nova ran as independent after split with ADI. EU Election Observation Mission deployed. 142,296 registered voters.

Parliament dissolved June 25 by King's Representative Sir Tom Marsters on PM's advice. 24 seats, first-past-the-post. Voter registration deadline approaching. Self-governing territory in free association with New Zealand. Sources: RNZ, PINA, Cook Islands News

14 presidential candidates confirmed by ECZ (June 29). Electoral reforms added 70 new parliamentary seats. Campaign schedule adopted. Key issues: jobs, cost of living, critical minerals, democratic concerns. PF joined UPND alliance (no PF on ballot per reports). Sources: ISS Africa, DW, ECZ, Mail & Guardian

SNAP ELECTION called July 1 by President Tokayev decree. First election under new Kurultai system. Ruling Amanat party renamed to Adilet in June 2026 merger with Asar. 98 Mazhilis seats + 69 maslikhat seats. Expected Adilet supermajority. Sources: Reuters, Astana Times, Times of Central Asia

EFFECTIVELY POSTPONED — No confirmed date. Originally targeted Aug 30, 2026. Key reasons: (1) Transitional Presidential Council (TPC) dissolved Feb 2026, leaving PM Alix Didier Fils-Aimé as sole executive authority; (2) Voter and candidate registration never began due to disputes between the Provisional Electoral Council (CEP) and PM over the electoral decree text; (3) PM designated CEP executive director as director general, concentrating control over electoral process in executive hands; (4) Electoral decree adopted June 2 but remains contentious; (5) Extreme security crisis — armed gangs control large parts of Port-au-Prince (BINUH report Jan-Mar 2026: 1,642 killed, 745 injured); (6) No candidates have formally registered. Gang Suppression Force operations ongoing but insufficient. Sources: UN Security Council Report (July 2026), BINUH, Reuters, Miami Herald.

Most closely watched German election of 2026. AfD polling near outright majority (~40-42%). CDU incumbent Schulze governs with SPD+FDP but both junior partners risk falling below 5% threshold. AfD state branch classified as confirmed right-wing extremist by domestic intelligence. AfD lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund. If firewall holds and AfD wins majority, they govern alone without needing coalition partners. Defence Minister Pistorius has discussed withholding classified info from potential AfD state ministers. Sources: Clean Energy Wire, TVP World, INSA, Politico

Riksdag election September 13, 2026. Left bloc (Social Democrats + allies) has significant lead. Andersson favored to become PM again. Immigration, defense spending, and Saab state ownership are key issues.

AfD leads as clear frontrunner (~30-35%). SPD incumbent Minister-President Manuela Schwesig personally popular but SPD weakened nationally. Same-day vote as Berlin (Sep 20). A second SPD defeat on same evening as Berlin would be devastating for Merz coalition junior partner. AfD unlikely to find coalition partners due to firewall but could complicate governance. Moscow-linked disinformation campaigns targeting eastern states reported (Euronews Jul 8). Sources: Atlantic Council, ING Think, DW

Highly fragmented five-way race. AfD topped a Berlin poll for first time (INSA Jul 23: 19%). CDU governing mayor Kai Wegner withdrew after scandal over handling of Jan 2026 power outage; replaced by Finance Senator Stefan Evers. Left Party competitive at 18%. First election with voting age 16. AfD unlikely to govern due to firewall but symbolic significance of leading in the capital. Sources: TVP World, INSA, rbb24, WSWS

Three-day voting (Sep 18-20). First Duma election since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Conducted under wartime conditions with significant restrictions on opposition. Sources: EPDE, RIDL, NEST Centre

incumbent: Aziz Akhannouch (PM, stepped down as RNI president; Mohamed Chouki is new RNI leader)
notes: Government allocated MAD 450 million for campaign funding (nearly triple 2021 levels). Coalition parties bracing for election battle. Akhannouch facing eroding public confidence. Sources: Morocco World News, Al Estiklal, Africa Intelligence
Two ballot measures: SVP neutrality initiative to enshrine neutrality in constitution, and food-related initiative. Per LeeWas poll, neutrality initiative faces disapproval.

incumbent: Denis Bećirović (Bosniak Chair), Željko Komšić (Croat), Željka Cvijanović (Serb)
notes: Rotating three-member presidency. Current chair: Denis Bećirović.

First round October 4, 2026. Lula seeking unprecedented 4th term at age 80. Flávio Bolsonaro (son of jailed ex-president Jair) carries PL banner. Romeu Zema (NOVO) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) also running. Lula leads in most polls but race tightening.
27 of 81 Senate seats up for election. Coincides with municipal elections. ANO (PM Babiš party) expected to gain seats.

President Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned Jul 24 2026 citing Autonomic Neuropathy. Per Article 123(2) of the Bangladesh Constitution a new president must be elected within 90 days of the vacancy (deadline: approx Oct 22 2026). The president is elected by members of parliament (Article 48). Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad discharging presidential duties per Article 54. BNP holds supermajority in parliament following Feb 2026 landslide. Sources: Bangladesh Constitution (bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd) BBC Al Jazeera Reuters

Knesset election October 27, 2026. Neither Netanyahu coalition nor opposition projected to secure 61-seat majority. Bennett's Together and Eisenkot's Yashar competing for anti-Netanyahu vote. Likud remains largest single party but coalition weakened.

CANCELLED: President Ortega announced Jul 20, 2026 there will be no more elections in Nicaragua. Consolidating power with co-president/wife Rosario Murillo. US Secretary of State Rubio condemned the move. UN Human Rights Council has accused regime of authoritarianism.

incumbent: Mike Johnson (Speaker), Chuck Schumer (Senate Majority Leader)
notes: Confirmed. All 435 House seats + 35 Senate races (33 regular + 2 special). Also 36 gubernatorial races. Key Senate battlegrounds: TX, OH, NC, AK, ME, MI. Democrats favored to flip House; Senate is a tossup. Referendum on Trump presidency. Sources: The Conversation, Cook Political Report, 270toWin, Ballotpedia

General election November 7, 2026. Both major parties at 30-year low. Hipkins preferred PM but Labour dropped 5 points. Opportunity Party nearing 5% threshold. Coalition government clings to slim majority.
Date not confirmed (tentative Oct 31 - Nov 15). Follows May 2026 parliamentary election won by PAICV (Francisco Carvalho becomes PM). Sources: IFES Election Guide, CGTN Africa
President Abbas issued decree on June 15, 2026 calling for legislative elections Nov 1, 2026 (presidential elections in early 2027). First PLC elections in 20 years. Per Le Monde, DW.

Elections for county magistrates, city mayors, county/city councilors, township mayors, and village chiefs. Key test of DPP popularity midway through President Lai's term. Date confirmed by Central Election Commission on Oct 31, 2025.

Presidential election expected autumn 2026. Incumbent Iliana Iotova (acting since Jan 2026 after Radev resigned). Progressive Bulgaria (Radev) dominates after April parliamentary landslide. Date not yet confirmed by CEC.

Confirmed December 5. Barrow describes election as unprecedented with four former VPs challenging him. Opposition coalition setting July 11 deadline to pick unified candidate. Sources: Kerr Fatou, Gambiana

incumbent: Transitional Military Council (Embaló ousted Nov 2025 coup)
notes: Embaló ousted in Nov 26, 2025 military coup. Junta proposed Dec 6, 2026 elections but date unconfirmed. Country suspended from CPLP and international bodies.
National Elections Commission declared Dec 22, 2026 as general election date (announced June 2026). First general election since independence in 2011. Per BBC, Eye Radio.

NOTE: Andy Burnham became PM on Jul 20, 2026 without a general election. He won the Labour leadership contest after Keir Starmer resigned Jun 22, 2026. UK's 7th PM in a decade. Next general election must be held by Jul 2029 but date not yet set. Burnham may call a snap election. Reform UK leads polls (24%) ahead of Labour and Conservatives (both 19%).
